doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Alfred Laine Interview, 1951-04-21

title: Seven bands before World War I and their names
summary: He ran up to seven bands until the first world war, named Reliance, Tuxedo and Lane, with split bands going out under the Lane name; some men were drafted.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yes, I've had the lawyer candidates, both. Son and father playing lots of jobs with me, but the first time when, when I first organized, they played, especially the old man. He was with me. He was one of my members of the first, first band. Now, I had, uh, all together, I used to master seven bands up, up until, uh, the war, the world's war, first world's war. And, of course, a lot of the men, they went with, uh, they were drafted, and went, of course, in the army. Did they all have your name,
Jack Lane's band? No, I had Reliance band,

one band named Reliance, the other name, Tuxedo, and the other name, Lane. Different names like that, you understand? And, of course, split bands, well, they'd go out all together, under the name of Lane, would be the split bands, you see? I wouldn't give them the right name, because they were from the different bands. I see. Members of the different bands. Well, then we'd carry on from there. Jack, what about the, uh, minstrels?
